correctness.rationale: For the face fan of Wu's coordinate box slice Q in the zero-sum lattice, the globally defined toric discrepancy is its gauge h(d)=max(max_i d_i/B,-min_i d_i/A). A nonzero integer zero-sum point has a positive integer coordinate at least 1, so h>=1/B, and primitive (1,-1,0,..) attains equality since A>=B. Hence global mld=1/B (centers anywhere, not pointwise local mld). The lattice interior criterion yields canonical iff B=1. When B=1, the same witness is a nonvertex boundary point except at n=2,A=1; there the only integral hexagon points are origin and six vertices, giving terminal iff (2,1,1). A=B+1 is coprime and valid for all n>=2, yielding alpha->1/2 and mld->0. Read actual RESULTS and discrepancy_verify.py; independently enumerated representative n,A,B lattice sections using rational gauge, not a proof of all n.
